angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 7,325,721 km at 28.23 pc = 3.47 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 148387: the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax the radius was computed with (Table 1), 35.42 +/- 0.09 mas, inverted (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aa9d8b): 28.233 +/- 0.072 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 35.7163 +/- 0.2829 mas (same row, RUWE 3.71), 126.2 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 10.53 +/- 0.04 solar radii from Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 148387: radius 10.53 +/- 0.04 solar radii (Table 5), from the limb-darkened angular diameter 3.47 +/- 0.01 mas (NPOI, Table 4) and the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aa9d8b): 7,325,721 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 2.45 +/- 0.1 solar masses from Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 148387: mass 2.45 +/- 0.1 solar masses (Table 6), from the PARAM Bayesian fit to PARSEC isochrones at the measured temperature; the paper calls its masses estimates only (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aa9d8b); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5060 +/- 64 K from Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 148387: effective temperature 5060 +/- 64 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aa9d8b). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 148387: effective temperature 5060 +/- 64 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aa9d8b)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/eta-draconis.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 2.782, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * eta Dra: spectral type G8-IIIab (1989ApJS...71..245K)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * eta Dra: projected rotation speed 0.26 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2024A&A...692A.189R)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Pulkovo spectrophotometric catalogue, table 5 (320-1080 nm, 2.5 nm steps, 10 nm resolution, absolute flux in W m^-2 m^-1)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
